text: . Prime Minister Narendra Modi today paid homage to the Indian Hockey Legend Major Dhyan Chand on the occasion of National Sports Day. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that Major Dhyan Chand’s brilliance in Indian hockey continues to inspire generations. Extending his greetings to all sports lovers, the Prime Minister said that their dedication, passion and determination make the nation proud.Union Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya also paid floral tribute to Indian hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand on the occasion of National Sports Day in New Delhi. Talking to the media, Dr Mandaviya said that National Sports Day is celebrated every year to commemorate the birth anniversary of Major Dhyan Chand.He said with the aim of taking the Fit India Movement forward, the ‘One Hour on the Playing Field’ programme has been organised across the nation. Dr Mandaviya also called upon everyone to spend at least one hour on the playing field every week and keep themselves fit and healthy. He emphasised that a fit youth and a healthy society are essential for building a prosperous nation.

. India has signed a deal with the US for the acquisition of Javelin anti-tank guided missile systems for the Indian Army. This marks India’s formal entry as a customer of the famed shoulder-fired weapon even as both countries work towards its eventual joint production in India. The US Embassy & Consulates in India, in a statement yesterday, said that the Indian Army had signed a Letter of Offer and Acceptance for the purchase of the Javelin.The embassy also said that the United States welcomes the Indian Army’s signing of a Letter of Offer and Acceptance for the purchase of the Javelin. US Ambassador to India, Sergio Gor, said the agreement demonstrated the depth of American support for the Indian Army and created new opportunities for our defence industries to work together.

. Ministry of External Affairs has said that 320 Indian nationals remain uncontactable or are reportedly missing following the flash flood tragedy on Wednesday.Addressing the media in New Delhi today, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that around 100 people of Indian origin, holding other nationalities also remain uncontactable.  He said, 63 Indian nationals working at the Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project were rescued from the affected area. He said, another 96 Indian nationals who were stranded on the Chinese side have safely crossed into Nepal by land and efforts are underway to evacuate them.Mr Jaiswal informed the media that twenty-one Indian nationals from Tamil Nadu, who had arrived in Kathmandu from the flood-affected area yesterday, have reached New Delhi this afternoon.On the Chinese side, Mr Jaiswal said that around 400 Indian nationals are safe and in contact with their families. He said, the Indian Embassy in Beijing is coordinating with local authorities, team leaders and travel agents to facilitate their evacuation.Mr Jaiswal also said that as requested by Nepal, India is preparing to send a Tunnel rescue team, for which a recce team is being flown in first to assess the equipment required there. He added that a medical team is also being sent and in addition to it , India has also offered Bailey bridges along with their associated technical teams so that connectivity can be restored quickly in the affected parts of Nepal. Mr Jaiswal said that India is ready to offer any other assistance that the Nepal authorities might require.Mr Jaiswal said that the government has set up a control room in the Ministry of External Affairs, which is working round the clock. He said, Indian embassies, both in Kathmandu and Beijing, have also set up 24 X 7 helplines.Meanwhle, the third flight carrying ten tonnes of humanitarian assistance has departed for Kathmandu. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar informed this in a social media post. The Minister said that the assistance includes portable generator sets, dignity kits, food packets and water purification tablets. Dr Jaishankar said that an 11-member team of doctors, paramedics and Recce team for Tunnel rescue operations is also on-board. He also reiterated India’s support to Nepal’s ongoing relief and rescue efforts. Earlier, India had sent more than 47 tonnes of emergency relief supplies in two flights.

. The Indian women’s hockey team ended their FIH World Cup campaign with a historic 3-1 win over higher-ranked Germany in the fifth-place classification match at Amstelveen, Netherlands, yesterday. The fifth-place finish is India’s best performance at the World Cup in 52 years, since the team finished fourth in the inaugural edition in 1974. The achievement is even more impressive, as the current squad included 11 World Cup debutants. For India Ishika opened the scoring in the 43rd minute, followed by two quick goals from Navneet Kaur in the 44th and 47th minutes.Germany’s Lynn Krings scored a late consolation goal in the 59th minute. India lost only one match in the tournament, going down 0-2 to hosts and Olympic champions the Netherlands. The team also drew with China and England and defeated South Africa 6-1. After being eliminated from the semi-final race following a goalless draw against Australia, India bounced back strongly against Germany. Despite a slow start, India scored three goals in four minutes and defended firmly against Germany’s attacks. The performance will give the team a major confidence boost ahead of next month’s Asian Games in Japan.

. Union Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that India cannot become a Visksit Bharat without a Viksit Punjab. He assured the farmers of Punjab that the Central Government would not compromise with their interests. He said every agreement signed with any country will be done by keeping their welfare in mind first.Addressing farmers and others at Baba Bakala in Amritsar district during the Rakhar Punya programme yesterday, he said opposition parties, including the Aam Aadmi Party is spreading false narratives that the Central government is signing agreements against the interests of the farmers, but this is not the case. Chouhan said the Centre is committed to ensuring that farmers benefit from its welfare schemes. Mr Chouhan said that under the leadership of the Prime Minister, Punjab has received central support of more than 8 lakh 20 thousand crore rupees under various schemes.These include PM Kisan Samman Nidhi, PM Awas Yojana, PM Jan Dhan, MSP for farmers and fertiliser subsidy. He said that for the development of villages in the state, 1,331 crore rupees have been given this year under the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (G RAM G Yojna). The Union Minister specifically blamed the Punjab government for not implementing Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), which would have compensated the farmers who were affected in last year’s floods in the state.He said the centre is trying to do everything possible for the welfare of Punjab farmers through various schemes, but the AAP government in the state is becoming a roadblock in implementing them. He accused both the Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party of failing to undertake concrete work for the welfare of farmers and the common people. He also criticised the state government for the deteriorating law and order situation and drug menace in Punjab.

. The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has expanded the Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID)-based silver hallmarking ecosystem with 341 silver Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs) across 102 districts, and more than 25,000 silver jewellers are registered with BIS ahead of the festive season. The BIS informed that since the launch of the Silver HUID portal on 1 September last year, over 77 lakh silver jewellery pieces have already been hallmarked with HUID.The six-digit HUID under the Hallmarking System Assures Traceability of Silver Jewellery and Artefacts. The BIS advised consumers purchasing silver jewellery to look for the BIS hallmark and verify the HUID through the BIS CARE app. It also advised to purchase only hallmarked silver jewellery from BIS Registered Jewellers to be assured of its purity. Further, the BIS urged consumers to also obtain a proper invoice for the purchase of silver articles and retain it for future reference.

. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan has extended his greetings on the occasion of National Sports Day today. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan paid tribute to Indian Hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand and said that the spirit of determination, discipline and excellence defines Bharat’s sporting culture. He noted that the nation’s growing sports ecosystem reflects the commitment to nurturing talent at every level.Mr Radhakrishnan said that Indian athletes continue to shine on the global stage, bringing laurels to the nation and inspiring the next generation to aim higher. The Vice President also called for renewed efforts to promote fitness, encourage greater participation in sports and inspire young Indians to pursue excellence with dedication and perseverance.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange color warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Odisha during the next two to three days. Heavy rainfall is also likely to prevail over Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, East Madhya Pradesh, Gangetic West Bengal, Uttarakhand and the northeastern parts of the country till tomorrow.Meanwhile, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Andhra Pradesh, North Interior Karnataka, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are expected to witness thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds today. IMD has also forecast squally weather with wind speed gusting to 65 kilometres per hour likely to prevail off the south Tamil Nadu coast, south-west Bay of Bengal and a few parts of the Arabian Sea for the day.

. Grand Master Trilok Subba from Sikkim has been selected to represent India at the World Taekwondo Poomsae Championship. Akashvani correspondent reports that internationally acclaimed Taekwondo player Grand Master Trilok Subba, from Sikkim, has been selected to represent India at the World Taekwondo Poomsae Championship in Chuncheon, South Korea.The Championship is scheduled to take place from 16th to 20th September. Subba will compete in the Under-60 Male Individual Poomsae and team events in the Senior category. Prior to this selection, Subba clinched a gold medal for the National Team at the National Taekwondo Poomsae Championship held in Maharashtra in July 2026. Mr Subba will leave Sikkim shortly to join the National Camp in Maharashtra & then he will travel to South Korea for the Championship.

. Hockey Bengal will organise its Annual Awards Ceremony 2026 in Kolkata today to mark National Sports Day and the 121st birth anniversary of legendary hockey player Major Dhyan Chand. The ceremony will honour players, coaches, umpires, journalists and organisations for their contribution to the development of hockey in Bengal. National Sports Day is observed on August 29 in memory of Major Dhyan Chand, a three-time Olympic gold medallist and one of India’s greatest hockey players.

. Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh today informed that around 440 space technology startups are registered in India. In a written reply in Lok Sabha, Dr Singh said Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre, IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities, NGEs to carry out various space activities. Out of these, 18 NGEs are start-ups. The Minister said the Government has undertaken several proactive measures following the liberalization of the space sector. This is being done to promote participation of startups in satellite manufacturing, launch services, downstream applications and space-based technologies. IN-SPACe is facilitating the transfer of available ISRO technologies to industry while also identifying and consolidating the technology requirements of industry for future technology development and transfer. Till date, 118 Technology Transfer Agreements have been executed.

. The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) has achieved a major milestone in its nationwide mission-mode drive for Mandatory Biometric Updates, completing more than two crore biometric updates for school children across the country. The special drive, initiated in September last year, has now covered over one lakh 56 thousand schools, enabling school children to complete their Aadhaar biometric. Electronics and IT Ministry said that this has helped Mandatory Biometric Updates service to reach children directly at their schools, making the process more accessible and convenient for crores of students.Aadhaar enrolment for children below five years captures demographic information and a photograph, while fingerprints and iris biometrics are not captured at that age as these biometrics are still developing. Mandatory Biometric Updates helps ensure that the child’s Aadhaar continues to have updated biometric information. The Biometric updates are required when a child attains the age of 5 years and again at 15 years. To encourage timely completion and make the service more accessible, UIDAI had waived the charges for  children in the 7 to 15 years age group from 1st October 2025, for a period of one year. The Ministry said that lack of Biometric Updates in Aadhaar may lead to difficulties while carrying out authentication for receiving benefits under various Government schemes, registering in competitive and university examinations.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uzbekistan tomorrow. He will be on a two day visit to Tashkent city. During the visit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President of Uzbekistan, Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev, will review cooperation in different sectors.India and Uzbekistan have relations that go back to ancient history. India was one of the first countries to recognise the state sovereignty of Uzbekistan after the latter’s independence. India and Uzbekistan elevated their relationship to a strategic partnership in 2011. Since then, bilateral relations have expanded substantially across a wide range of areas.The Prime Minister’s visit will reaffirm the close, multi-faceted, and growing strategic partnership between India and Uzbekistan. Discussions are expected to cover a wide range of areas of mutual interest and identify new avenues for strengthening bilateral cooperation.This engagement will provide an opportunity to highlight the long-standing cultural ties between India and Uzbekistan, as well as the important role of academic and people-to-people exchanges in further strengthening bilateral relations.

. On National Sports Day today, Nagaland Chief Minister Neiphiu Rio said the state celebrates the dedication and perseverance of its sportspersons and recognises the role of sports in promoting fitness, discipline and teamwork. In a post in X, Mr Rio called upon all stakeholders to continue strengthening the state’s sporting ecosystem and inspire a culture of active living, inclusivity and excellence. Meanwhile, in commemoration of National Sports Day 2026, the Directorate of Youth Resources and Sports, Nagaland, will honour meritorious sportspersons for 2025-26 this morning at a programme to be held in Kohima.

. Secretary (West), External Affairs Ministry, Sibi George met Member of the European Parliament Ondřej Dostál and exchanged views on bolstering India-EU joint collaboration across trade, business, health, green tech, culture and academic sectors. In a social media post, External Affairs Ministry said they also discussed ways to further expand the bilateral relations between India and the Czech Republic.

. The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has completed ten years of transforming digital payments and has emerged as the backbone of India’s digital payments ecosystem. The UPI, which was launched on 25th August 2016, has surged almost 13 thousand fold in transaction volume. The Finance Ministry said that the annual transaction volume expanded from just 1.78 crore transactions in 2016-17 to over 24 thousand 162 crore transactions in 2025-26. The transaction value also rose sharply from seven thousand crore to nearly 314 lakh crore during the same time period. The Ministry said that UPI has also emerged as a global platform for cross-border digital payments and is currently operational in 11 countries. These are United Arab Emirates, France, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Singapore, Mauritius, Qatar, Cambodia, Greece and Maldives.UPI has emerged as one of the most successful pillars of India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, providing an interoperable, real-time payments platform. Today, it is the preferred mode of payment for millions of users, transforming the way India transacts. By bridging the digital divide, advancing financial inclusion, and expanding access to digital financial services, UPI has empowered individuals and communities across the country while driving broad-based economic participation. The unprecedented scale and reliability achieved by UPI have received global recognition. It said, the International Monetary Fund has acknowledged it as the world’s largest real‑time payment system. As of 2025, UPI accounts for nearly 49 per cent of the world’s real-time payment transaction volume.

. The Tata Institute of Social Sciences, TISS, conferred degrees on 1,376 students and scholars at its 86th annual convocation held in Mumbai yesterday.The degrees included those awarded to 35 doctoral scholars and graduates from Master’s, Bachelor’s, Integrated and dual-degree programmes.The first undergraduate batch of Analytics and Sustainability Studies also received their degrees. Director of Tata Memorial Hospital, Dr C. S. Pramesh, was the chief guest at the convocation.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will share his thoughts with the people of the country and abroad in the Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani at 11 AM on Sunday. It will be the 137th episode of the monthly radio programme. The programme will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani and Doordarshan network, the AIR News website, and the Newsonair mobile app. It will also be live-streamed on the YouTube channels of AIR News, DD News, the PMO, and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Akashvani will broadcast the programme in regional languages immediately after the Hindi broadcast.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the Jan Dhan Yojana has delivered unprecedented scale and transformative outcomes, with an unparalleled impact in the last 12 years. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that Jan Dhan Yojana is playing a significant role in advancing financial inclusion and empowering people across the country. Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, more than 59 crore accounts have been opened so far, with total deposits amounting to 3 lakh 17 thousand crore rupees. The scheme was launched by Prime Minister Modi on this day in 2014. As the world’s largest financial inclusion initiative, the scheme continues to redefine access to banking for all Indians. Under the scheme, 78 per cent of the accounts have been opened in rural or semi-urban areas, and approximately 56 per cent of accounts are owned by women.

. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan will undertake a three-day visit to Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Keralam and Lakshadweep, beginning tomorrow. During his visit, the Vice President will participate in a series of programmes encompassing education, public service, cultural heritage, industry-academia collaboration, fisheries outreach and major public celebrations.Mr Radhakrishnan will attend the Founder’s Day Celebration of the Kongu Vellalar Institute of Technology Trust at Erode, TamilNadu tomorrow. Later in the day, the Vice President will travel to Bengaluru, where he will attend the centenary celebrations of former Karnataka Chief Minister Ramakrishna Hegde at the Vidhana Soudha.On Sunday, the Vice President will visit Keralam, beginning with Alappuzha, where he will attend the 115th anniversary celebrations of Kerala Kaumudi. Further, he will proceed to Pathanamthitta to inaugurate the Aranmula Water Festival 2026. Later, Mr Radhakrishnan will travel to Thiruvananthapuram, where he will inaugurate the Onam Pageantry, marking the celebrations of Keralam’s major cultural festival.On the last day of his visit, the Vice President will visit Agatti in Lakshadweep, where he will attend an Outreach Programme organised by the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. Returning to Keralam, he will attend the Silver Jubilee Celebrations of Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology and the Confluence 3.0 Industry-Academia Summit in Kakkanad, Kochi.

. India’s Industrial output growth, as measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), expanded by 6.7 per cent in July this year on an annual basis. The July data indicates that industrial activity continued to expand at a healthy pace, although the pace of growth moderated from the revised June level.The sharp upward revision in June’s IIP growth to 8.8 per cent from 7.3 per cent also indicates that the industrial momentum entering the July quarter was stronger than initially estimated. According to government data, Manufacturing, which carries the heaviest weight in the index, grew by 7.3 per cent, while electricity and gas supply posted an 8.7 per cent expansion in July. Water supply, sewerage and waste management rose by 7.4 per cent. However, the mining sector proved to be a laggard, posting a negative growth of 0.9 per cent last month.

. Global crude oil prices eased today. Brent crude was trading half a per cent down at 89 US dollars and 30 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.8 per cent lower at 82 US dollars and 84 cents per barrel when reports last came in.

. All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi has introduced a new course titled GARBHINI MITRA to Strengthen Ayurveda-Based Maternal Wellness Support for the 2026-2027 academic session.The Ministry of AYUSH said that the six-month course is designed to develop trained personnel to provide appropriate health education, lifestyle guidance, and community-level support to women during pregnancy and the postnatal period.The ministry noted that Candidates of 18 years or above, who have passed the Senior Secondary examination from any recognized board are eligible to apply before its last date that is 31st August.Once completed, candidates can work as Garbhini Mitra Assistants, Prenatal or Postnatal Care Assistants, Antenatal Wellness Guides and Maternal Health Support Workers, across different Ayush centres, maternity clinics and wellness institutions.The course inculcates traditional ayurvedic concepts of Garbhini Paricharya, Sutika Paricharya and Garbhadhana Vidhi.

. India’s foreign exchange reserves surged by 12.4 billion US dollars (USD) to a record high of 729.3 billion US dollars during the week ended August 21.According to the Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, increased by 9.4 billion USD to 591.3 billion USD during the week. Gold reserves added 2.8 billion USD to 114.2 billion US dollars. Special Drawing Rights rose by 112 million USD to 18.8 billion USD.Country’s reserve positions with the International Monetary Fund added 26 million USD to around 4.9 billion USD.

Mr Radhakrishnan will attend the Founder’s Day Celebration of the Kongu Vellalar Institute of Technology Trust at Erode, Tamil Nadu, today.Later in the day, the Vice President will travel to Bengaluru, where he will attend the centenary celebrations of former Karnataka Chief Minister Ramakrishna Hegde at the Vidhana Soudha. . Prime Minister Narendra Modi has left for his four-day visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic this morning. In his departure statement, Mr Modi expressed confidence that his visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic will strengthen India’s strategic partnerships in Central Asia and deepen the civilisational connection with the region. He said that in recent years, the India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership has seen significant advancement.The Prime Minister said that he is looking forward to having discussions with the President of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, on further deepening cooperation in trade and investment, digital connectivity, defence, and energy, and on advancing the shared visions of Viksit Bharat and Yangi Uzbekistan. Mr Modi said that he will also visit the Shastri Memorial and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies, which is a tribute to the close cultural and people-to-people ties that bind the two countries.The Prime Minister said that at the invitation of the President of the Kyrgyz Republic, Sadyr Zhaparov, he will travel to Bishkek to participate in the 26th SCO Summit. Mr Modi said that he is looking forward to advancing India’s vision for the region, anchored in Security, Connectivity and Opportunity, and to working with fellow members for a region free from the scourge of terrorism, separatism and extremism, which continue to threaten peace and stability in the neighbourhood and beyond. The Prime Minister said that during his visit to the Kyrgyz Republic, he will also meet President Zhaparov and other SCO leaders and will attend the Opening Ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games.

. The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana has completed 12 years today, marking a significant milestone in transforming the country’s financial inclusion landscape. The scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on this day in 2014. Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, more than 59 crore accounts have been opened so far, with total deposits amounting to 3 lakh 17 thousand crore rupees.As the world’s largest financial inclusion initiative, the scheme continues to redefine access to banking for all Indians. The average deposit per account is 5,356 rupees. Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, 78 per cent of the accounts have been opened in rural or semi-urban areas, and approximately 56 per cent of accounts are owned by women. Over 41 crore RuPay cards have been issued to Jan Dhan account holders. The scheme has also empowered millions, particularly the marginalised sections, to access banking and financial services to improve their socio-economic conditions.The Jan-Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity, with Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana at its core, has proven to be a diversion-proof mechanism for the direct delivery of financial assistance. Due to initiatives like Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, India’s Financial Inclusion Index has risen from 53.9 in 2018 to 67 in 2026, showcasing deeper access to credit, insurance, savings and digital payments. As the world’s largest financial inclusion initiative, the scheme is redefining access to banking for millions of underprivileged citizens.

. India’s Velavan Senthilkumar won the PSA Budapest Squash Open title in Hungary after defeating home favourite Balazs Farkas 3-0 in the final. He had an impressive run to the title, beating World No. 18 and Asian Games gold medallist Eain Yow Ng 3-0 in the quarterfinals before overcoming fellow Indian Veer Chotrani 3-2 in a thrilling semifinal. Senthilkumar capped his remarkable week with a dominant performance in the final.

. The results of the UGC National Eligibility Test (NET) for 84 subjects have been announced, with more than 4,000 candidates qualifying for the Junior Research Fellowship. The National Testing Agency (NTA) had ordered fresh examinations for candidates who appeared for the English, Commerce and Sociology papers in June this year after an expert committee found factual, typographical, translation and language-related errors in the question papers.The NTA released the UGC-NET answer key on August 16, nearly two months after the examination, while issuing a special notice concerning the Sociology, Commerce and English papers. Later, on the same day, it announced that the three examinations would be conducted afresh in September, citing the errors. The re-examinations are scheduled for September 9 and 10, for which candidates will not be required to pay an additional fee.

. Khelo India Dialogue programmes were held in various locations across Mizoram to encourage students and young athletes to pursue sports and improve their performance in line with changing times. As part of the initiative, Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the Khelo India Dialogue through video conferencing yesterday, outlining ways in which sports could contribute to the country’s development.Prime Minister Modi said sports should not be viewed merely in terms of winning medals but also as a means of building a stronger and more united India. He stressed the importance of regular physical exercise and urged participants to maintain a healthy mind and practise self-discipline. In Aizawl, the NSS Unit of Government Aizawl North College organised a programme where resource person Dr T. Lalremruata highlighted the importance of teamwork, unity and self-discipline in sports. A similar programme was held at Government Champhai College, where NSS Programme Officer Lalventluanga spoke about various opportunities for the development of students and athletes and interacted with the participants.In Hnahthial, the programme was organised at Government Higher Secondary School with the assistance of Khelo India Judo Instructor Zomuansanga. A total of 127 students, including 67 boys and 60 girls, took part in the event. At Government Saitual College, Khelo India Saitual District Representative Laltleipuia said children were being trained and encouraged to pursue sports under the Khelo India initiative. He said football and wrestling training for children was also being conducted intensively in Saitual district under the programme.

. Global crude oil prices rose moderately today. Brent crude was trading 0.7 per cent up at 88 US dollars and 50 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.4 per cent up at 82 US dollars and 50 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. The Government has said that there is no shortage of sugar in the country and all necessary measures will be taken for adequate availability of sugar at reasonable prices. The Consumer Affairs Ministry said that ex-mill sugar prices have declined by around 20 per cent in recent days, while retail sugar prices have also started coming down.The Ministry said it has taken a series of proactive measures to ensure adequate availability of sugar and prevent artificial tightening of supplies in the domestic market. The Government has been closely monitoring sugar prices, stocks and movement across the country. It has decided to introduce a fortnightly sugar allocation system from next month, replacing the existing monthly quota system to ensure that sugar reaches the market in a timely manner.

. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that India is fast emerging as a global platform for manufacturing, innovation and exports. She urged Canadian investors to tap the country’s growing potential to serve both domestic and international markets. She said, India’s reform-led transformation and strong growth trajectory are creating opportunities for a more resilient and investment-driven India-Canada economic partnership.Addressing a high-level Business Roundtable in Toronto yesterday, Sitharaman highlighted that reforms, digitalisation, infrastructure investment and targeted policy support were steadily strengthening the environment for long-term investment in the country. She invited Canadian companies and investors to view India not merely as an investment destination, but as a strategic partner and platform for global growth. She encouraged businesses to establish long-term operations and partnerships that can serve both the Indian market and international markets.The Finance Minister also highlighted opportunities for Canadian companies in financial services, particularly through the Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City) International Financial Services Centre (GIFT IFSC).  With ambition to raise two-way trade to 70 billion dollar annually by 2030, Sitharaman emphasised that the India-Canada economic opportunity extends far beyond trade, encompassing investment, technology, innovation, financial services and long-term global partnerships.

. As many as 37 pilgrims from Maharashtra who were stranded in Tibet after flash floods in Nepal departed for Kathmandu this morning. According to the Maharashtra Chief Minister’s Office (CMO), the group left Saga in Tibet at around 6 am via the Nyalam check-post and is travelling safely towards the Nepalese capital. The pilgrims are from Thane, Pune, Raigad, Alibag and Dombivli.Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis’s office said the MEA promptly extended assistance to facilitate the group’s movement. Earlier, Maharashtra’s Disaster Management Department said at least 114 people from the state were stranded in the Himalayan nation, with 53 confirmed safe.

. Indian Grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa created history, becoming the first Indian to win the Grand Chess Tour after staging a stunning comeback to defeat defending champion Fabiano Caruana 15-13 in the final at St. Louis in the US last night. Praggnanandhaa started the final day six points behind Caruana but won both rapid games to take the lead.He then held his ground in the four blitz games to seal a 15-13 victory, claim 2 lakh dollar first prize and also secure a guaranteed spot in next year’s Grand Chess Tour. In the third-place match, Wesley So also made a strong comeback against Vincent Keymer. After the players shared the rapid games, So won all four blitz games to seal an 18-12 victory. Earlier, Praggnanandhaa had lost the first classical game to Caruana 6-0 but drew the second game 3-3, keeping his hopes alive.

. Ahead of Independence Day, a platform for creative expression has been provided to the youth in Uttar Pradesh. For this, the ‘Rang De Basanti’ campaign was launched. Under this campaign, the graffiti wall programme organised near Lucknow University today. Artists from the city painted public murals on the theme of a mafia-free and changing Uttar Pradesh. Through these paintings, the Uttar Pradesh of before 2017 and the changes that have taken place in Uttar Pradesh thereafter were portrayed.On the wall, artists used their colours and imagination to portray in paintings the changed positive environment in the state in terms of law and order, infrastructure and opportunities for youth. Young painter Manish Saroj’s painting expressed the pain of Uttar Pradesh suffering under mafia rule before 2017, while also presenting a positive picture of the change taking place now.Under the campaign, a comic distribution and dialogue programme will be organised in Muzaffarnagar tomorrow. During this, an original comic based on communal harmony will be distributed. Along with this, dialogues will also be held with youth in schools. On August 14, the song ‘Azadi from Fear’ of the ‘Rang De Basanti’ campaign will be launched. It will also feature a confluence of rap, music and digital art.

External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar today bid farewell to outgoing Ambassador of the European Union to India Hervé Delphin.In a social media post, the Minister appreciated the outgoing Ambassador’s contributions towards concluding the India-EU FTA and further strengthening the Strategic Partnership. He wished him the best for his future endeavours.

In a special conversation with Akashvani News, India’s Ambassador to Uzbekistan, Smita Pant, said that the relations between the two countries are strengthening rapidly, and during the Prime Minister’s visit, there will be a discussion on increasing cooperation in all areas. She said that business between the two countries has increased manifold in the last few years, and during the Prime Minister’s visit, both countries will discuss improving connectivity and reducing bottlenecks.There is considerable discussion about important decisions on cooperation in rare earth minerals during the Prime Minister’s visit.  Smita Pant said that Uzbekistan is rich in natural resources, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Tashkent will also discuss investment and technology transfer in the mining and rare earth minerals sectors. The ambassador said Bollywood plays a vital role in strengthening relations between Uzbekistan and India, and Uzbekistanis are passionate about Indian films, serials, and film stars. Smita Pant stated that the two countries may take some important decisions to enhance cultural contacts during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit.

Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has said that the country today stands as an important place of transformation and renewed confidence, showcasing the results of collective determination and efforts. The Vice President said this after releasing a book titled Sankalp Se Siddhi ka Modi Yug written by Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari. He said that whether it is advancing technology, building modern infrastructure, and strengthening national unity and promoting women-led development, education is the tool for empowerment. Mr Radhakrishnan also highlighted the contributions of the country’s youth, women, farmers, workers, and every citizen for their involvement in building a stronger and prosperous nation. He also underlined that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the only leader in the world to provide free Covid-19 vaccines not only to 140 crore Indian people but also to hundred more countries.Speaking about the book, the Vice President said that through the publication, the author seeks to bring together many aspects of country’s larger narratives, reviving pride in cultural heritage and enhancing the country’s voice at the global stage. He added that the book reflects the journey of the nation and encourages everyone and boosts their enthusiasm.

. The Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) price has been hiked by Rs 3.89 per kilogram in Delhi-NCR. With today’s price hike, CNG in the national capital now costs 86 rupees 98 paise per kilogram. The revised CNG prices have come into effect from 6 AM today.Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL) has said that even after this revision, the CNG retail price in Delhi continues to be amongst the most economical options for consumers. IGL said that due to the re-escalation of the West Asia crisis since July this year, CNG consumption is witnessing a significant jump in line with the fast-growing Indian economy and surging consumer demand. The company said these factors have resulted in a considerable increase in input gas cost for the CNG segment.

As many as 290 people from Maharashtra stranded in different parts of Nepal following devastating flash floods have been confirmed safe, while 60 others remain untraceable, a state government official said today.Of the 395 Maharashtra residents confirmed to have been in Nepal during the disaster, 105 are already on their way back to India, while the state control room has established contact with the remaining 290, who are safe but stranded.The 60 untraceable tourists were part of a Nepal tour organised by Mumbai-based Richa Tours Pvt Ltd.Meanwhile, 37 Maharashtra pilgrims stranded in Tibet after completing the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra left for Kathmandu today  morning following intervention by Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.

. The Publications Division of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has received seven awards at the Federation of Indian Publishers (FIP) Awards for Excellence in Book Production, 2026. The Division’s journals, books and reference publications in Hindi, English and Urdu have been recognised in various categories.Director General, Publications Division, Dr. Dhiraj Kakadia said that the books and journals published by the Division play an important role in bringing diverse and valuable content related to national development, literature, culture, art and contemporary issues to readers. He said, the seven awards received by the Publications Division are a testament to the collective hard work, dedication and excellence of its officers and personnel.

. Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju will be leading the Indian delegation for the High-Level Commemorative Meeting in Belgrade, Serbia, from 31 of this month till 1st of September. The theme for the Meeting is ‘The Legacy of Non-Alignment: Lessons for Today’s World’. The External Affairs Ministry, in a statement, said that the meeting marks the 65th Anniversary of the First Conference of Heads of State or Heads of Government of the Non-Aligned Movement. The Ministry noted that India is a founding member of the movement, which brings together 121 developing countries on a platform of historical significance. It added that India remains committed to the principles and values of the movement.

In Men’s Cricket, the second and final Test between India and Sri Lanka ended in a draw, with the hosts at 429 for 9 in their second innings on the fifth and final day in Colombo.Despite the draw, the Shubman Gill-led side clinched the two-match series 1-0.Batting first in the second Test, India declared at 503 for 9 before bowling Sri Lanka out for 290 to secure a 213-run first-innings lead. The visitors enforced the follow-on, but Sri Lanka showed remarkable resilience in their second innings. They reached 429 for 9, taking a lead of 216 runs, before both captains agreed to call off the match.

. The death toll from devastating flash floods in Nepal and Tibet has risen to 579, with 1924 people still missing. According to the data released by Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, 579 bodies have been recovered so far, while 101 injured people are undergoing treatment in hospitals. The missing figure of 1,924 includes people from hydropower projects, foreign nationals, civilians and security and government personnel.As many as 933 people from hydroelectric projects are reported missing, while 517 foreign nationals remain unaccounted for. Meanwhile, India has stepped up humanitarian assistance to Nepal affected by flash floods as the third flight carrying 10 tonnes of humanitarian assistance departed for Kathmandu last evening. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar yesterday told the media that India is supporting Nepal in ongoing relief and rescue efforts. The Ministry of External Affairs has said that 320 Indian nationals remain uncontactable or are reportedly missing following the flash flood tragedy on Wednesday.

. Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Bhatti Vikramarka has directed Singareni officials to explore a joint venture with Karnataka’s Hatti Gold Mines for future gold mining projects. He gave these instructions during a visit to the Hatti and UTI gold mines in Raichur district, Karnataka, on the second day of his tour to the region.The Deputy CM, who also holds the Finance and Energy portfolios, said combining the technical expertise of both public sector companies could improve India’s domestic gold production. He noted that Hatti Gold Mines has vast experience in gold exploration, mining, processing and refining, and suggested that Singareni’s technical skills in coal and mineral mining be combined with this experience. Bhatti Vikramarka said gold plays a key role in the country’s economic security, and government companies like Singareni should take the lead in scientifically exploring domestic gold reserves to reduce import dependence.During the visit, he inspected the production unit, mineral processing centre and electro-winning unit at Hatti Gold Mines. Officials told him the project currently produces two to four kilograms of gold daily. He also visited the UTI open-cast and underground gold mines, and asked officials about mining technology, transport and worker safety. Singareni CMD Dr Buddha Prakash Jyothi and other senior officials accompanied him on the tour.

. Secretary (Economic Relations), External Affairs Ministry, Sudhakar Dalela interacted with an official delegation from Ethiopia, Sierra Leone, Malawi, Zambia, Rwanda, and African Union Commission. United Nations Development Programme in India coordinated the visit.In a social media post, External Affairs Ministry said that they discussed harnessing digital public infrastructure for development, governance, empowerment, inclusion and delivery of citizen-centric services. It said, India stand ready to share its development experience of deploying digital public infrastructure at population scale across sectors with partners in Africa.

. India’s double Olympic medallist Neeraj Chopra has qualified for the 2026 Diamond League final, which will be held in Brussels next month. Chopra accumulated 12 points in the standings. Chopra had finished fourth at the Doha meet in June with a throw of 85.69 metres before recording a season-best 88.05 metres at the Lausanne meet earlier this month, where he finished second. Chopra is sixth in the standings after competing in two Diamond League meets this season. Chopra’s two performances were enough to secure a place in the Diamond League final.
